### Simple note-taking for your everyday thoughts. Memos is an open-source, self-hosted note-taking app that brings your everyday thoughts together in a personal timeline. Your data stays yours, and you choose what to keep private or share. [Demo](https://demo.usememos.com) · [Install](#quick-start) · [Docs](https://usememos.com/docs) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/tfPJa4UmAv) ## About Memos Memos is an open-source, self-hosted note-taking app for your everyday thoughts. - **Everyday writing.** A single sentence can be a whole memo, or you can take your time with a longer entry, using Markdown to give your words more structure. - **A personal timeline.** Each memo stays with the day you wrote it, bringing your thoughts together in a timeline you can look back through. Tags connect related thoughts across those days, making it easy to pick up a topic again or find something you remember writing. - **Your own data.** Your record lives on your own server, and your data stays yours. - **Sharing you control.** You choose what stays private, what to share with family and friends, and what to publish on the web. In shared spaces, you can write alongside others while each person keeps their own memos. ## Quick start With Docker installed, run: ```bash docker run -d \ --name memos \ -p 5230:5230 \ -v ~/.memos:/var/opt/memos \ neosmemo/memos:stable ``` Open http://localhost:5230 and create the first account. Everything Memos keeps is in `~/.memos`, so back up that one folder. Other ways to run Memos, including Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and a plain binary, are in the [deployment guide](https://usememos.com/docs/deploy). ## Upgrading Releases are tagged `YY.MM.N`, with release candidates as `YY.MM.N-rc.K` and no `v` prefix. The Docker tag `stable` follows stable releases, a month tag such as `26.10` follows the newest stable release of that month, and `canary` follows development builds. Coming from a release before v0.31.0, run [v0.31.0](https://github.com/usememos/memos/releases/tag/v0.31.0) once first; see the [upgrade requirements](store/migration/README.md). ## Around Memos - [Web Clipper](https://usememos.com/web-clipper) for [Chrome](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/memos-web-clipper/nebaoebnljalfegiidibihhkebeiklbl) and [Firefox](https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/memos-web-clipper/) saves pages, selections, and images to your memos as Markdown with a link to the source. - [Memogram](https://github.com/usememos/telegram-integration) is a Telegram bot that saves your messages and images to Memos. - The [API](https://usememos.com/docs/api/latest) and [MCP server](https://usememos.com/docs/integrations/mcp) connect Memos to your own scripts and AI tools. ## Sponsors

      

Sponsor Memos through [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/usememos). ## Help and contributing Questions go to the [docs](https://usememos.com/docs), [Discord](https://discord.gg/tfPJa4UmAv), or [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/usememos/memos/discussions). Bugs and ideas go to [issues](https://github.com/usememos/memos/issues/new/choose). Code changes start with the [contributing guide](https://usememos.com/docs/development/contributing). ## Star History

## License Memos is open source under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
readmeHtml:
✨ Featured sponsor: CodeRabbit — Industry-leading AI code reviews.

Simple note-taking for your everyday thoughts.

Memos is an open-source, self-hosted note-taking app that brings your everyday thoughts together in a personal timeline. Your data stays yours, and you choose what to keep private or share.

Demo · Install · Docs · Discord

About Memos

Memos is an open-source, self-hosted note-taking app for your everyday thoughts.

  • Everyday writing. A single sentence can be a whole memo, or you can take your time with a longer entry, using Markdown to give your words more structure.
  • A personal timeline. Each memo stays with the day you wrote it, bringing your thoughts together in a timeline you can look back through. Tags connect related thoughts across those days, making it easy to pick up a topic again or find something you remember writing.
  • Your own data. Your record lives on your own server, and your data stays yours.
  • Sharing you control. You choose what stays private, what to share with family and friends, and what to publish on the web. In shared spaces, you can write alongside others while each person keeps their own memos.

Quick start

With Docker installed, run:

docker run -d \
  --name memos \
  -p 5230:5230 \
  -v ~/.memos:/var/opt/memos \
  neosmemo/memos:stable

Open http://localhost:5230 and create the first account. Everything Memos keeps is in ~/.memos, so back up that one folder.

Other ways to run Memos, including Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and a plain binary, are in the deployment guide.

Upgrading

Releases are tagged YY.MM.N, with release candidates as YY.MM.N-rc.K and no v prefix. The Docker tag stable follows stable releases, a month tag such as 26.10 follows the newest stable release of that month, and canary follows development builds. Coming from a release before v0.31.0, run v0.31.0 once first; see the upgrade requirements.

Around Memos

  • Web Clipper for Chrome and Firefox saves pages, selections, and images to your memos as Markdown with a link to the source.
  • Memogram is a Telegram bot that saves your messages and images to Memos.
  • The API and MCP server connect Memos to your own scripts and AI tools.

Sponsors

      

Sponsor Memos through GitHub Sponsors.

Help and contributing

Questions go to the docs, Discord, or GitHub Discussions. Bugs and ideas go to issues. Code changes start with the contributing guide.

Star History

License

Memos is open source under the MIT License.

releases.body:
Memos 26.11.0 fixes typing Japanese and Korean in Safari and makes attachment failures visible instead of opaque. The server cache and upgrades from v0.31 deployment files are also more reliable.

## Fixes and polish

* **Editor:** Typing Japanese or Korean in Safari no longer selects the first word of a new line while the input method is composing. ([editor 26.11.0](https://github.com/usememos/memos/commit/c2f1699e031602fb5fcd8bad314120301e5f8009), [#6517](https://github.com/usememos/memos/issues/6517))
* **Attachments:** When an attachment cannot be read, the server answers with a JSON error instead of labelling it as the file's own type, so a PDF that fails to load no longer reaches the browser's viewer as a broken document. Missing local files return 404, and every failure is logged with its cause. ([#6516](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6516), [logged failures](https://github.com/usememos/memos/commit/3feb08737bfa831fdb6a4500bed8ec5e0cf257b6))
* **Server:** The in-memory cache keeps its entry count exact and no longer drops a fresh write when an expired entry under the same key is removed at the same moment, so it stays within its size limit under load. ([#6513](https:

Memos 26.10.0 adds a rich editor that shows a memo as it will look while you write, per-user usage limits, and declarative configuration for operators. Browsing, Markdown rendering, sign-in, security, and the server improve throughout, and releases now use calendar versions.

## Highlights

* **Editor:** Memos opens in a rich editor by default: text looks the way the saved memo will, with a toolbar over selected text, a slash menu, and Markdown shortcuts. Markdown mode in the ＋ menu keeps the raw text, now saved to your account under Settings › Editor; focus mode opens a narrower sheet with larger text. releases.body:
Memos 26.10.0-rc.2 brings a new editor that writes and reads memos the same way, per-user usage limits, and calendar versioning. Sign-in, browsing, Markdown rendering, and the server improve throughout.

### What's new

* **Editor:** Writing and reading share one block editor, so a memo looks the same while you type and after you save. Format with the toolbar over selected text, the slash menu, or Markdown shortcuts. Markdown mode in the ＋ menu edits the raw text and is remembered per device; focus mode opens a narrower sheet with larger text. releases.name: 26.10-rc.1
releases.body:
Memos 26.10-rc.1 adds contextual editor suggestions, transcription for existing audio attachments, and a unified way to browse by creator and Space. Markdown, Calendar and Map views, image previews, and navigation receive improvements throughout the app.

### What's new

* **Editor suggestions:** New memo drafts offer tags, checklist formatting, and visibility choices based on the current filters or selected View. Suggestions are optional and disappear once fulfilled. ([#6367](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6367))
* **Audio transcription:** Transcribe an existing audio attachment from the memo editor using the configured transcription provider. The transcript is inserted into the draft for review and saving; existing text and the original audio are preserved. ([#6375](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6375))
* **Browsing:** Keep the selected creator and Space while switching between Timeline, Calendar, Map, and Attachments. The attachment library includes files from memos you can read and shows their uploaders. ([#6378](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6378))

releases.name: v0.31.0
releases.body:
Memos 0.31 adds Spaces for collaboration, Calendar and Map views for browsing your notes, and tools to move your memos between instances. Writing, search, attachments, and navigation also receive improvements throughout the app.

## Highlights

* **Spaces:** Organize memos in shared Spaces, invite people through their inbox, move memos between Spaces, and choose custom icons or emoji. Space-only visibility limits a memo's audience to active Space members, with the administrator access described below. ([#6228](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6228), [#6266](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6266), [#6285](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6285), [#6287](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6287))
* **Calendar and Map:** Browse memos by month, open a day to read or add notes for that date, and explore memos with location data on a dedicated map. aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, self-hosted note-taking application designed for quick capture and Markdown support.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Memos is a self-hosted note-taking application built around a timeline-first interface to facilitate rapid thought capture. It prioritizes data ownership by allowing users to deploy the application on their own infrastructure, ensuring no telemetry or external data collection occurs. The tool natively supports Markdown for formatting and offers a lightweight footprint, available as a single Go binary or a Docker container. It provides flexibility by supporting multiple database backends, including SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, and offers REST and gRPC APIs for custom integrations. This creates a secure, highly personal knowledge base alternative to cloud services.
keyFeatures: Timeline-First Interface: Provide a simple, feed-like view for capturing and reviewing notes quickly without complex categorization overhead.
Data Ownership: Ensure complete privacy by running entirely on self-hosted infrastructure with absolutely no telemetry.
Flexible Deployment: Run as a single Go binary or a Docker container, supporting SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL for data storage.
Markdown Native: Natively support Markdown syntax for formatting notes, ensuring compatibility and ease of use.
API Integrations: Expose both REST and gRPC APIs, allowing developers to build custom tools and integrations on top of the platform.
Lightweight Architecture: Design to consume minimal system resources, making it suitable for low-power personal servers and homelabs.

useCases.title: Personal Knowledge Management
useCases.description: Individuals use the timeline interface to rapidly capture daily thoughts, links, and ideas without worrying about folder structures.

useCases.title: Private Journaling
useCases.description: Privacy-conscious users host the application locally to maintain a secure, private digital journal that cannot be accessed by third parties.

useCases.title: Custom Tool Integration
useCases.description: Developers utilize the exposed REST APIs to build automated note-taking workflows or custom frontend clients.

useCases.title: Low-Resource Deployment
useCases.description: Homelabbers deploy the lightweight Docker image alongside SQLite on a Raspberry Pi for a highly efficient note-taking solution.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Memos is designed for individuals, developers, and privacy advocates who want a fast, self-hosted alternative to cloud-based note-taking apps. Users should be comfortable with basic deployment methods like Docker or running standalone binaries.
